method: Plates are loaded symmetrically: the target total minus the bar weight is split in half, and each half must be built from the pairs on the rack, counting one plate per pair on each side. The calculator searches every combination of the listed pairs in the unit's own increments - 25, 20, 15, 10, 5, 2.5 and 1.25 kg, or 45, 35, 25, 10, 5 and 2.5 lb - and reports the exact target when it is reachable, preferring the combination with the fewest plates and repeating one plate size before mixing sizes. When the target is not reachable it reports the nearest lighter and heavier totals the rack can build, with the shortfall or surplus, rather than rounding silently. A full rack is four pairs of every size; pair counts can be lowered to model plates already on another bar. Because the load must balance, a difference whose hundredth of a unit cannot split in two is refused, as are targets outside 500 kg or 1,100 lb, bars above 100 kg or 220 lb, bars of zero, and non-integer pair counts. Collars, clips and bar flex are excluded, and the tool performs loading arithmetic only - not lifting, training or safety advice. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network requests.
